title: Ancient Trees in India: Places to Explore
meta_description: A Kolkata banyan that lives on 4,208 prop roots, a Mumbai fig that closed over its railings, a Gujarat shrine under a banyan. {trees} trees across {places} places in India.
intro: The Great Banyan in Howrah has had no trunk since 1925, when a fungus forced its main stem to be cut out, and it carries on standing on 4,208 prop roots that the Botanical Survey of India has counted one by one. It is the largest tree we map in India, and most of the others are on the same pattern, figs that grow sideways. In Gujarat, a village shrine to the goddess Mahakali sits under a banyan that locals call Mini Kabirvad, after the famous one on an island in the Narmada. In Mumbai, a fig in Mahim has fused its roots around an iron railing and a tiled offering platform until only the rusted arrowheads show. In Delhi, a peepal stands on a stone plinth beside a banyan near Humayun's Tomb. The rain trees of Bengaluru, Mangaluru and Parel came from tropical America and were planted for shade along colonial roads, and a few now carry a tree house. Almost every tree here was sent by a reader who stopped under it, so ages are mostly unknown and we say so rather than guess.
